main_text.p: eis subiicitur, & in quo vnum eorum alterū pellit. Hoc autem tertium rerum naturalium principium materia est & potestate ens, atque patibile. Verūtamen quæcunque oriuntur eodem modo oriri, non necesse est. Quædā enim vt substantiæ, simpliciter fiunt, eo quod ante fui ortū simplicitas non erant. Cum enim homo oritur, tum nondum est. Alia vero ἀπὸ τι fieri dicuntur, vt ea, quæ accidentia sunt, quorum ortus nō simpliciter sit & absolutus. Nam homo, cum musicus sit, tum est, sed non musicus. Itaque in huiusmodi generatione non acquiritur substantia, sed dunta-xat aliquod accidēs, qualis est musica ars, quę aduenit homini. Sed in substantiæ generatione non solùm comparatur accidens, sed etiā substantia. Cæterùm in vtraque generatione, vt & in illa eorū, quæ arte cōstant, semper materiam subiici, necesse est, quæ ab aliis naturæ principiis distinguitur. Est enim ens duntaxat potestate, & corporeæ substantiæ pars, atque eorum omniū quæ natura oriuntur velut mater. Priuatio verò, quanuis in ipsa infit materia, nullius substantiæ pars est, eò quòd accidens sit, & substātiæ corruptionem moliatur. Etenim corruptionis naturalium corporū maximè in causa est, propterea quòd formæ aduersetur. Est enim formæ absentia in materia. page.notes: Several long-s and ligature forms are rendered with plain s as instructed. Greek word "ἀπὸ τι" is a best reading of a damaged Greek phrase at "vero ... ri fieri"; the glyph is an uncertain Greek abbreviation and should be checked: [?] applies to the Greek and the transcription may not be exact. Several words in the scan are hard to read at the damaged left edge and gutter (e.g. "simpliciter"/"simplicitas", "non nondum", "substantiæ", "substātiæ") and should be verified against the original. The middle of line "non erant" / "Cum enim homo oritur, tum nondum est" was partly obscured by a fold; the printed line reads "tum nom est" with the letters partly hidden, so "nondum" is a reconstruction. Lines near "quæ accidentia sunt" and "substantiæ" in the 6th-7th paragraph lines are blurred. The page is a single paragraph running over from the previous page and ending mid-sentence with the catchword "in" at the foot.
